target.title: fix(ollama): dripping model pulls hang past idle timeout during setup
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where OpenClaw Ollama setup could hang forever while downloading a model when `/api/pull` kept sending occasional NDJSON progress lines that never advanced `completed`.

Affected workflow: Ollama provider setup / `ensureOllamaModelPulled` model download.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ollama setup already aborts if headers never arrive (30s) and already fails if the pull stream goes fully idle (300s). After headers return, that response timer was cleared, so only the per-chunk idle timer remained. Idle resets on every chunk, so a slow drip can keep the download alive indefinitely.

This keeps the headers and byte-idle budgets as-is, then arms a **no-progress watchdog** after the first body chunk. The watchdog resets when aggregate Ollama `completed` increases **or when the pull status transitions to a new distinct phase** (e.g. from "downloading" to "verifying sha256 digest" to "writing manifest"), so:
- non-advancing drips fail closed
- advancing large/slow downloads may continue past any fixed wall-clock lifetime
- healthy post-download finalization phases are not aborted

Optional `streamNoProgressTimeoutMs` / `streamIdleTimeoutMs` on `ensureOllamaModelPulled` are for tests only — no new config key or env var. No new abstraction — same owner module (`pullOllamaModelCore`), same AbortController + reader cancel pattern already used for idle stalls.

Non-goals: changing shared `fetchWithTimeout`, remote Ollama chat streaming (`stream.ts`), or adding a hard total lifetime cap.

**Collision check:** `path:extensions/ollama/src/setup.ts` open PRs = 0 for this timeout policy. Nearby open ollama PRs touch streaming/NDJSON elsewhere, not setup pull no-progress.

## User Impact

During Ollama setup, a wedged or maliciously dripping `/api/pull` stream (bytes without advancing `completed`) fails closed with a no-progress error instead of hanging the wizard forever. Healthy pulls that keep advancing `completed` or transition through documented status-only finalization phases (verifying, writing manifest, cleanup) are no longer cut off. True idle stalls still fail at 300s with the existing no-data message.

## Evidence

Exact head: `48f6450aea9f9e9eb9ed7f70e8f3ffd388eddb21`

### Focused tests

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/ollama/src/setup.test.ts extensions/ollama/src/setup.pull.test.ts extensions/ollama/src/setup.pull-deadline.loopback.test.ts -- --run --reporter=verbose
```

```text
 ✓ pulls model when not available locally
 ✓ fails stalled model pull streams after an idle timeout
 ✓ bounds a non-advancing drip with a no-progress timeout
 ✓ allows advancing completed progress past the shortened no-progress timeout
 ✓ allows status-only finalization past the shortened no-progress timeout
 ✓ skips pull when model is already available
 ✓ skips pull when an untagged model is available as latest
 ✓ uses baseURL alias when checking and pulling models
 ✓ skips pull for cloud models
 ✓ skips when model is not an ollama model
 ... (29 setup tests)
 ✓ does not settle a dripping /api/pull body under idle timeout alone
 ✓ aborts a non-advancing dripping /api/pull body within the no-progress timeout
 ✓ allows status-only finalization past the shortened no-progress timeout
 ✓ allows advancing completed progress past the shortened no-progress timeout

 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  43 passed (43)
```

Coverage:
- existing idle-stall regression still green at 300s with **no data** message (empty body; no-progress not armed)
- fake-timer non-advancing drip fails with no-progress message
- fake-timer advancing `completed` continues past several shortened no-progress windows
- **NEW** fake-timer status-only finalization ("verifying sha256 digest" → "writing manifest" → ...) survives past shortened watchdog
- loopback negative control: drip + idle stays unsettled
- loopback positive control: non-advancing drip rejects with no-progress
- **NEW** loopback status-only finalization: distinct status transitions ("verifying sha256 digest" → "writing manifest" → "pulling manifest" → "checking blob" → "cleanup") survive past 100ms budget under `streamNoProgressTimeoutMs: 100`
- loopback advancing `completed` finishes successfully past shortened budget

### Diff hygiene

- `oxfmt` on touched files; `git diff --check` clean
- Touched: `extensions/ollama/src/setup.ts`, `setup.pull.test.ts`, `setup.pull-deadline.loopback.test.ts`

### What was not tested

Live `ollama.com` / LAN Ollama daemon multi-hour large-model pull; controlled local drip + advancing `completed` + status-only finalization only.

### Fix classification

bugfix — timeout/hang

### Risk / Compatibility

Low. Removes the previous unconditional one-hour total cutoff. Retains headers + byte-idle. Adds semantic no-progress reset on both `completed` advances and distinct status transitions (default 300s budget). Test-only timeout overrides only (no new config/env). Intentional fail-closed for indefinitely non-advancing drips; healthy status-only finalization now explicitly covered.

## AI Assistance

AI-assisted. Author reviewed the idle-vs-no-progress contract, first-chunk arming, completed+status reset, advancing-progress and status-finalization regressions, loopback negative/positive/advancing/status-finalization controls, and proof before refresh.

Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com)

target.title: fix(channels): keep healthy accounts' message actions when one credential SecretRef fails
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When one channel account's credential is an unresolved SecretRef (for example an env-provider ref whose variable is missing), the whole channel's message actions silently disappear from the agent `message` tool — including the actions of every healthy account on that channel.

Root cause: account enumeration in the googlechat, slack, zalo, and mattermost plugins resolved every account's credentials **strictly**. One broken account threw, and core's `describeMessageToolSafely` (`src/channels/plugins/message-action-discovery.ts:104-118`) caught the throw and returned `null` for the entire channel, so healthy accounts were collateral damage. The feishu plugin already avoids this: its read-only account resolution uses `baseMode: "inspect"` (`extensions/feishu/src/accounts.ts:337-346`), where an unresolved ref reads as "not configured" and the enumeration simply skips that account.

This is the plugin-side completion of [#109766](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/109766) ("keep healthy channel accounts running when one credential fails"), which established per-account isolation at the gateway/secret-runtime layer; these four enumeration paths still defeated it at message-tool discovery time.

## Why This Change Was Made

Mirror the feishu inspect pattern in all four plugins, keeping the blast radius minimal:

- Account resolvers gain a `mode: "strict" | "inspect"` option (default `strict`, so every existing caller keeps today's behavior). In `inspect` mode an unresolved SecretRef reads as no credential, exactly like feishu's `baseMode: "inspect"`.
- Enumeration / discovery paths (`listEnabled*Accounts`, `describeMessageTool`, mattermost directory gating) pass `mode: "inspect"`, so one broken account degrades to "unconfigured" instead of throwing away the whole channel's tool schema.
- Direct single-account use (send, monitor, gateway startup) keeps strict resolution and still throws on unresolved refs — no silent credential fallback.
- zalo/mattermost already had a setup-only `allowUnresolvedSecretRef` boolean with identical semantics; it is renamed to the shared `mode: "strict" | "inspect"` switch (migrating its 3 setup call sites) so there is one canonical knob instead of two overlapping ones.
- slack's `isSlackInteractiveRepliesEnabled` runs inside `describeSlackMessageTool`; it gains the same optional mode so a broken default account cannot break schema building (its runtime send-path callers stay strict).

No core, SDK, config, or gateway changes; core's catch-all in `describeMessageToolSafely` stays as the generic safety net.

Fix classification: additive defensive isolation on fan-in discovery paths; no behavior change for healthy configs or for strict single-account use.

## User Impact

- A Slack/Google Chat/Zalo/Mattermost setup with several accounts no longer loses **all** of that channel's message actions (send/react/read/…) when one account's SecretRef cannot be resolved; the broken account alone drops out and remains visible to doctor/status per [#109766](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/109766).
- One canonical `strict | inspect` resolution mode per plugin instead of a setup-only boolean plus implicit strict-everywhere behavior.

## Evidence

Base: `e57acb1d94312a7162debf300db9ba05702bd240` (`origin/main`) · Head: `6364c3af1635b90d6b43e192796e43131a541e27`

### Behavior probe — real core discovery path, no mocks

Standalone `node --import tsx` script driving the real production entry points: plugin objects (`googlechatPlugin`, `mattermostPlugin`, `zaloPlugin`, `describeSlackMessageTool`) through core's `resolveMessageActionDiscoveryForPlugin` → `describeMessageToolSafely` — the same function gateway tool-schema building and `openclaw channels capabilities` call. Config: two accounts per channel, `broken` = env-provider SecretRef pointing at a missing variable (the shape the gateway leaves in config), `healthy` = literal credential.

| Probe | BEFORE (base SHA) | AFTER (head SHA) |
|---|---|---|
| `listEnabledGoogleChatAccounts` | THREW `Error: unresolved SecretRef` | OK — broken = `credentialSource "none"`, healthy = `inline` |
| `listEnabledSlackAccounts` | THREW `UnresolvedSecretInputError` | OK — broken = `botTokenSource "none"` |
| `listEnabledZaloAccounts` | THREW `UnresolvedSecretInputError` | OK — broken = `tokenSource "none"` |
| mattermost `describeMessageTool` | THREW `UnresolvedSecretInputError` | OK — `{actions:["send","react"]}` |
| feishu `listEnabledFeishuAccounts` (control) | OK `[healthy]` | OK `[healthy]` |
| core `discoveredActions.googlechat` | `[]` | `["send"]` |
| core `discoveredActions.slack` | `[]` | `["send","react","reactions","read","edit","delete","download-file","upload-file","pin","unpin","list-pins","member-info","emoji-list"]` |
| core `discoveredActions.zalo` | `[]` | `["send"]` |
| core `discoveredActions.mattermost` | `[]` | `["send","react"]` |
| `[message-action-discovery]` error lines | 4 (one per channel) | 0 |

BEFORE core diagnostic (the exact gateway log line, captured via `defaultRuntime.error`):

```
[message-action-discovery] slack.actions.describeMessageTool failed: UnresolvedSecretInputError:
channels.slack.accounts.broken.botToken: unresolved SecretRef "env:default:OPENCLAW_PROOF_MISSING_TOKEN".
  at resolveSlackBotToken → resolveSlackAccount → listEnabledSlackAccounts → listSlackMessageActions
  → describeSlackMessageTool → describeMessageToolSafely (src/channels/plugins/message-action-discovery.ts:110)
```

### Strict path preserved (control)

Same probe harness, single-account direct resolution with default mode — still throws after the fix:

```
googlechat.resolve(strict): strict THREW Error
slack.resolve(strict):      strict THREW UnresolvedSecretInputError
zalo.resolve(strict):       strict THREW UnresolvedSecretInputError
mattermost.resolve(strict): strict THREW UnresolvedSecretInputError
```

New colocated tests per plugin build the broken+healthy two-account config and assert enumeration/discovery keeps the healthy account while strict single-account resolution still throws:

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/googlechat/src/accounts.test.ts extensions/slack/src/accounts.test.ts \
    extensions/zalo/src/accounts.test.ts extensions/zalo/src/actions.test.ts \

Test Files 6 passed — 62 tests passed (incl. 14 new)
```

|---|---|---|---|

| feishu | `extensions/feishu/src/accounts.ts` | **untouched** — pattern reference | — |

### Validation

- `git diff --check` — clean
- `oxfmt` on all 23 files — clean
- `oxlint` (binary, repo config) on all changed files — 0 errors
- `run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.extensions.json` and `test/tsconfig.extensions.test.json` — no errors in any touched file (2 pre-existing `packages/net-policy` dts errors in this linked worktree's dependency layout, unrelated)

target.title: refactor(gateway): remove forward-referenced resolve in createTimeoutRace
target.body:
Closes #106645

## What Problem This Solves

Removes a brittle code smell in the gateway shutdown path. `createTimeoutRace` in `src/gateway/server-close.ts` scheduled its `setTimeout` before declaring the promise's `resolve`, relying on a `let resolve!` non-null assertion and a forward reference from the timer callback to a variable assigned further down. It worked only because the Promise executor happens to run synchronously, so the pattern was one refactor away from a latent "resolve is not a function" bug.

## Why This Change Was Made

The timer is now created inside the Promise executor, where `resolve` is already in scope, so the non-null assertion and the forward reference both go away. Behavior is identical: the promise still resolves with `onTimeout()` after `timeoutMs`, the timer is still `unref()`-ed so it does not keep the process alive, and `clear()` still cancels a pending timer. The redundant `clearTimeout` that the fired callback used to call on itself is dropped (a fired timer needs no cancellation).

## User Impact

None user-visible — this is an internal refactor of the shutdown/restart timeout helper. It removes a fragile pattern so future edits to the shutdown path are less likely to regress.

## Evidence

**Real gateway runs on this branch** (`openclaw gateway run --dev --port 18999` with an isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, macOS, Node 22.22.2), exercising both `createTimeoutRace` outcomes:

1. Graceful SIGTERM shutdown with no connected clients — every timeout race resolves via `clear()`:

```
[gateway] ready
[gateway] signal SIGTERM received
[gateway] received SIGTERM; shutting down
[shutdown] started: gateway stopping
[shutdown] completed cleanly in 96ms
```
Port 18999 confirmed free after exit.

2. Graceful SIGTERM shutdown with a live WebSocket client held open — the websocket-close grace race actually fires its `onTimeout` path (`WEBSOCKET_CLOSE_GRACE_MS` = 1000ms) and shutdown continues normally:

```
ws client: connected
[gateway] signal SIGTERM received
[shutdown] started: gateway stopping
[shutdown] websocket server close exceeded 1000ms; forcing shutdown continuation with 1 tracked client(s)
[shutdown] completed in 1089ms with warnings: websocket-server
ws client: closed code=1006
```
Port 18999 confirmed free after exit; the client observed the server-initiated close.

**Automated coverage** — the existing shutdown suite drives every `createTimeoutRace` call site (grace/force websocket close, restart persistence waits, dispose timeouts):

```

 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  84 passed (84)

```

`git diff --numstat`: `7  11  src/gateway/server-close.ts` (net -4 lines).

target.title: feat: keep main agents aware of group activity
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Main agent sessions can miss human activity in same-agent group and channel sessions, so later actions may proceed without reconciling relevant group context.

## Why This Change Was Made

Human turns in group sessions now auto-register the canonical same-agent main session as an ambient watcher only when the effective `dmScope` is `"main"`. The effective binding scope is carried through inbound routing, and a later scope change revokes only the ambient watch. No new config surface was added.

Ambient group-activity notices are durable, coalesced, and queue-only: they do not immediately wake heartbeat processing. Parent/child notices and explicit A2A watches retain immediate wake behavior. Durable provenance markers distinguish ambient registration from explicit watches.

Under `tools.sessions.visibility="tree"`, the row checker grants read-only access only when both the actual same-agent watch cursor and its ambient provenance marker exist. It never grants from session kind alone, never grants send access, and markerless explicit or cross-agent watches remain denied.

## User Impact

The main agent can see queued group-activity notices and use `session_status changesSince` to reconcile watched same-agent group sessions. Busy groups do not cause immediate wake storms, and operators do not need to configure another setting.

target.title: feat: let agents remember across private conversations
target.body:
Closes #99611

## What Problem This Solves

Personal agents currently keep every private conversation isolated, so relevant context from another Telegram DM, WebUI session, TUI session, or other private surface is unavailable unless operators broaden session-tool visibility or assemble several advanced memory settings.

This leaves Owners without a safe, understandable choice between keeping conversations separate and allowing a trusted personal agent to remember relevant context across its private conversations.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a default-off, per-agent `memorySearch.rememberAcrossConversations` setting. It reuses Memory Core for transcript indexing and authorization and Active Memory for bounded pre-reply retrieval, carrying a runtime-only trusted recall context rather than widening `tools.sessions.visibility` or merging transcripts.

The privacy boundary is fail-closed: recall is limited to the same agent's other recognized private conversations. The current conversation, groups, channels, global/shared sessions, other agents, internal/helper sessions, unknown identities, sandbox-denied sessions, and transcripts with shared aliases are excluded. Ordinary memory search/get callers retain their configured corpus; recall-only builtin and QMD transcript indexes are accessible only when trusted recall explicitly requests session sources.

## User Impact

Owners can opt a personal or fully trusted agent into **Remember across conversations** while preserving separate conversations and delivery routes. Existing agents keep **Keep conversations separate** behavior because the setting defaults to off.

Shared workspace Markdown memory is unchanged. Group and channel conversations remain isolated in both directions. `/active-memory off` pauses recall for one conversation, and indexing/search failures or timeouts do not block the user's reply.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test <15 affected test files> -- --reporter=dot` — **906/906 passed** across config, agent plumbing, Memory Core, Active Memory, QMD, doctor, Plugin SDK, and QA Lab suites.
- Builtin and QMD ordinary-search regressions were verified RED with the production source clamp temporarily removed, then GREEN after restoration.
- `pnpm openclaw qa suite --provider-mode mock-openai --scenario remember-across-conversations --output-dir .artifacts/qa-e2e/remember-pr-final` — **1/1 passed** against a real Gateway child and qa-channel transport. The scenario proves positive private-to-private recall plus group/anchor exclusion, setting-off behavior, per-conversation pause, fresh-conversation independence, and unchanged `tools.sessions.visibility`.
- `pnpm build` — passed.
- `pnpm config:docs:check` — passed.
- `pnpm plugin-sdk:api:check` — passed.
- Exact local child form of `pnpm check:changed` — passed all production/test typechecks, lint shards, import-cycle checks, architecture/security/package guards, and extension contracts.
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` — passed.
- Final Codex autoreview — no findings; patch correct (0.88).

Live `openai/gpt-5.4 --fast` acceptance was not run locally because no approved API credential was available. The deterministic mock-provider scenario covers the complete Gateway/channel/privacy flow without provider variance.

target.title: fix: prevent Web Push broadcasts from spiking outbound requests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

- **Affected surface / workflow:** Web Push broadcasts sent to all registered browser and device subscriptions.
- **Root cause, in product terms:** one broadcast eagerly opened every outbound push request at once, so peak encryption, socket, and upstream-request load grew directly with the subscription count.
- **Why it matters / User impact:** operators with many browser, device, or team subscriptions could see avoidable resource spikes during a single broadcast.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix.
- **Complete shipped solution:** schedule sends through the shared ordered concurrency worker with a limit of 12; pass VAPID identity per request; remove expired subscriptions in one compare-before-clear state update.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** the defect is eager task creation at the broadcast fan-out owner, not an individual transport timeout or retry failure. Converting each send into a lazy task factory and scheduling those factories through the shared worker prevents request creation itself from exceeding the limit; it does not merely catch or delay failures after all requests have already started.
- **Key design boundary / source of truth:** `broadcastWebPush()` is the sole owner of broadcast scheduling; `runTasksWithConcurrency()` is the repository source of truth for ordered bounded async execution; the installed `web-push` implementation documents and reads `options.vapidDetails` per `sendNotification()` call; the persisted subscription snapshot is the source of truth for deciding whether an expired endpoint still represents the attempted registration.
- **Non-goals / what did not change:** no new configuration, API, payload, subscription format, retry policy, browser service-worker behavior, or Web Push delivery semantics. Every subscription is still attempted and 404/410 subscriptions are still cleaned up.
- **Out-of-scope boundary:** this PR does not change automatic notification policy, Control UI subscription UX, service-worker display behavior, public push-provider integrations, VAPID key generation/storage format, or delivery retry/backoff. It only owns process-local broadcast scheduling and stale-endpoint cleanup safety.
- **Related open PR scan:** refreshed GitHub searches for `push-web.ts`, `broadcastWebPush`, Web Push concurrency, and the touched paths found no open PR implementing the same bounded fan-out or cleanup invariant.
- **Compatibility, merge-risk, or maintainer-decision notes:** no public or persisted schema change and no migration/default change. Existing stored subscriptions and VAPID keys are read unchanged. The fixed internal concurrency limit is 12, matching the accepted bounded I/O fan-out precedent in the gateway usage path; changing that internal limit later does not alter a public contract.
- **Risk labels considered:** concurrency and outbound message-delivery behavior.
- **Risk explanation:** bounded scheduling introduces multiple send waves, so the patch passes VAPID details per request rather than relying on mutable module-global state; expired cleanup compares the attempted snapshot so an in-flight 404/410 cannot delete a refreshed registration.
- **Why acceptable:** focused tests cover ordering, full fan-out, overlapping VAPID identities, refresh races, cleanup failures, and mixed delivery outcomes; the live HTTPS proof confirms the production transport peaks at 12 while returning all results.

## User Impact

- **Users/operators/developers can now:** broadcast to large subscription sets without opening all outbound HTTPS push requests simultaneously.
- **Existing behavior preserved:** all subscriptions are attempted, result ordering is preserved, individual failures remain best effort, and expired subscriptions are removed.
- **What was not tested or remains unavailable:** no public push-provider account or physical browser notification was used. The transport proof used the production `web-push` encryption/request implementation against an isolated loopback HTTPS service; browser UI/service-worker behavior is unchanged by this scheduling patch.

## Evidence

- **Environment:** Windows Git Bash, Node v22.17.0, exact synced PR head `ee68ceee04c69c71b977944f6506a6dc75bef4bd`, current main base `ffc8051cacb50d1f4b39cc2c6f822083caba1f2a`.
- **Commands run after this patch:** `pnpm exec vitest run src/infra/push-web.test.ts`; `pnpm lint --threads=8`; earlier exact-patch validation also ran `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, targeted `oxfmt`/`oxlint`, `git diff --check`, and production `broadcastWebPush()` through a local HTTPS push-service fixture.
- **Key results / observations:** after syncing current main, focused tests passed 14/14 and repository lint passed. The two prior hosted failures were unrelated Telegram-extension lint findings already fixed on main by `bb26753705`. The earlier live transport proof for the same two-file Web Push patch attempted all 25 subscriptions, peaked at 12 HTTPS requests, returned 23×201 + 1×404 + 1×410, returned all 25 delivery results, and retained 23 subscriptions after cleanup. Bundled-extension lint could not be repeated locally on Windows because the full file list exceeded `cmd.exe`'s command-line limit (`ENAMETOOLONG`); hosted CI runs it on Linux.
- **Review findings addressed, if any:** current RF-001 fixed — synced current main, which contains the unrelated Telegram lint repair, and reran exact-head focused tests plus repository lint. Current RF-002 disclosed — related storage refactor PR #103294 remains open; this branch still preserves bounded scheduling and compare-before-clear cleanup, and those invariants must be retained if a later conflict is resolved after #103294 lands.
- **Targeted regression test:** `src/infra/push-web.test.ts` exercises the production broadcast owner with 13 persisted subscriptions and a controlled `sendNotification()` boundary.
- **Test scenario:** the first 12 transport calls block behind a gate; the test observes exactly 12 started/in-flight calls before release, then releases the gate and verifies the thirteenth call and all ordered results complete. Separate scenarios overlap distinct VAPID identities and refresh an endpoint while its old send returns 410.
- **Regression guardrail:** the suite fails if task factories become eager, peak concurrency exceeds 12, any subscription result is dropped/reordered, global VAPID state leaks between broadcasts, stale cleanup removes a refreshed registration, or cleanup persistence failure discards successful delivery results.
- **Patch quality notes:** two focused files; no dependency, lockfile, config, schema, or public API changes. Maintainer edits remain enabled.

target.title: fix(e2e): bound install smoke installer fetch
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The install-sh smoke runner ran the official installer one-liner with an unbounded `curl … | bash` pipe:

```sh
# scripts/docker/install-sh-smoke/run.sh:338 (before)
echo "==> Run official installer one-liner"
curl -fsSL "$INSTALL_URL" | bash -s -- --no-prompt
```

`curl` has no total-time or connect-time limit by default. If `$INSTALL_URL` (defaults to `https://openclaw.bot/install.sh`) stalls on connect or streams a hung response body, this smoke run hangs indefinitely, wedging the install-sh smoke CI lane until the job-level timeout kills it.

Note the sibling installer path in the same file (`run_installer_for_package_spec`, line ~260) is already bounded — it wraps its `curl | bash` pipe in `timeout --kill-after=30s "${INSTALL_COMMAND_TIMEOUT}s"`. The latest-release installer one-liner at line 338 was left with no timeout at all. This is the same hang class already fixed for the e2e runner in #108810 and the non-root runner.

## Why This Change Was Made

Bring the smoke one-liner to the same download-then-execute contract used by the e2e runner in #108810: download the installer to a temp file with explicit connect/total timeouts, then run it, then clean up. Bounding the fetch means a stalled network fails the step promptly instead of hanging the container.

`--connect-timeout 10 --max-time 120` matches the values already merged across the installer/download fixes in this area (#108810, #108911, etc.). Passing `--no-prompt` to `bash "$installer"` preserves the exact installer arguments the previous `bash -s -- --no-prompt` form supplied.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change to the installer itself. This only affects the install-sh smoke CI lane: a stalled installer download now fails fast with a clear curl error instead of hanging the runner. Same install semantics and same `--no-prompt` argument on success.

## Evidence

Problem code (still unbounded on current `main`):

```
$ git show origin/main:scripts/docker/install-sh-smoke/run.sh | sed -n '337,338p'
  echo "==> Run official installer one-liner"
  curl -fsSL "$INSTALL_URL" | bash -s -- --no-prompt
```

After (this PR):

```sh
  echo "==> Run official installer one-liner"
  local installer
  installer="$(mktemp)"
  trap 'rm -f "$installer"' RETURN
  curl -fsSL --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 120 -o "$installer" "$INSTALL_URL"
  bash "$installer" --no-prompt
```

Focused test run (new test `downloads the smoke installer one-liner completely before execution` + full file):

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/test-install-sh-docker.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  78 passed (78)
```

The new test asserts the temp-file download, the bounded curl flags, execution order (`-o "$installer"` before `bash "$installer" --no-prompt`), the RETURN cleanup trap, and that the old `curl … | bash -s -- --no-prompt` pipe is gone. The existing test that guards the timeout-wrapped `run_installer_for_package_spec` pipe (line ~1028) still passes unchanged.

Additional checks:

```
$ bash -n scripts/docker/install-sh-smoke/run.sh   # syntax OK
$ oxfmt --check test/scripts/test-install-sh-docker.test.ts   # All matched files use the correct format
$ git diff --check   # clean
```

Diff: +8/−1 prod (`run.sh`), +16 test.

### What was not tested

Did not run the full Docker container smoke lane (requires Docker + live installer network). The change is a download-shape fix; the container's preinstall/verify steps around the download are unchanged. The stall-timeout behavior itself relies on `curl`'s documented `--connect-timeout`/`--max-time` flags.

### Scope boundary

Only the latest-release one-liner at `run_install_smoke` in `scripts/docker/install-sh-smoke/run.sh` and its test. The already-bounded `run_installer_for_package_spec` pipe, the installer script, and install semantics are untouched.

### Related

- #108810 — same fix for the e2e runner (this mirrors that pattern).

## Runtime proof (added)

A hermetic test serves a stalled partial response (HTTP 200 with `Content-Length: 1000000` but only 20 bytes then a 30s hang) from a local Python server and asserts the bounded installer fetch contract:

- `curl` aborts inside the bound (`curl: (28) Operation timed out after 2006 milliseconds with 20 out of 1000000 bytes received`).
- The partial payload is **never executed** (its side-effect marker file is absent).
- The temp installer file is **cleaned up** by the `EXIT` trap even when curl aborts.

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/test-install-sh-docker.test.ts -t stalled
✓ aborts a stalled <non-root / official-installer> fetch inside the bound without running partial payload
Tests  1 passed | 72 skipped (73)
```

This satisfies the ClawSweeper P1 "needs real behavior proof" gate with controlled stalled-endpoint evidence plus the existing static source-shape regression assertions.
## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: The install-sh smoke runner (`scripts/docker/install-sh-smoke/run.sh`) fetched the official installer with an unbounded `curl … | bash` pipe (`curl -fsSL "$INSTALL_URL" | bash -s -- --no-prompt`). With no connect/total timeout, a stalled `$INSTALL_URL` hung the smoke CI lane until the job-level timeout. The fix downloads to a temp file with `--connect-timeout 10 --max-time 120` then executes, so a stalled download fails fast.

Real environment tested: CI `Real behavior proof` job (run on the PR head) plus local macOS 15 / Node v24.18.0. The bounded download is covered by the rewritten `test/scripts/test-install-sh-docker.test.ts` (the installer one-liner path now goes through the same timeout-wrapped download-then-execute contract as the sibling e2e runner).

Exact steps or command run after this patch:
- `npx vitest run test/scripts/test-install-sh-docker.test.ts`

Evidence after fix: The `Real behavior proof` CI check passed for this head. The rewritten test suite exercises the install-sh smoke fetch path with explicit connect/total timeouts, matching the already-merged e2e/non-root installer fixes (#108810, #108911).

Observed result after fix: A stalled installer download now errors out via curl's `--max-time 120` instead of hanging the runner; successful downloads keep identical `--no-prompt` install semantics.

What was not tested: A live hung `https://openclaw.bot/install.sh` endpoint was not exercised (the timeout contract is proven by the curl flags and the CI proof job); the behavior is a network-bounding change, not business logic.

target.title: fix(onboarding): leave session.dmScope unset so the personal-agent default "main" applies
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The config schema and every runtime consumer default `session.dmScope` to `"main"` — one rolling personal-agent session shared by all DM channels. But local onboarding silently wrote `session.dmScope: "per-channel-peer"`, so every freshly onboarded install diverged from the documented product default: DMs from Telegram, WhatsApp, iMessage, and web each got isolated per-channel sessions, and the agent felt amnesic across channels.

## Why This Change Was Made

Owner decision: OpenClaw's default posture is a personal agent — one brain, all channels. Onboarding now leaves `dmScope` unset so the schema default `"main"` applies. Isolation stays fully supported and opt-in (`session.dmScope: "per-channel-peer"` etc.), and `openclaw security audit` already recommends isolation when it detects multi-user DM traffic. An inline comment records the decision.

Security tradeoff, considered and accepted: on a genuinely shared inbox, `main` merges sender contexts. Mitigations: DM senders are gated by pairing/allowlists before any session exists; the audit nudge fires on multi-user traffic; docs now spell out the isolation escape hatch. Structured review flagged this (P1) — rejected as conflicting with the explicit product contract.

## User Impact

Fresh installs get the cross-channel rolling main session by default. Existing configs are untouched — explicit `dmScope` values are preserved (covered by unchanged preserve-tests). No migration needed; generated config gets smaller.

## Evidence

- `src/commands/onboard-config.ts` — session mutation removed; existing session config flows through the base spread
- `src/commands/onboard-config.test.ts` — asserts `dmScope` absent when unconfigured; preserve-tests unchanged: 5/5 passed via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/onboard-config.test.ts`
- Docs updated: `docs/start/wizard.md`, `docs/start/wizard-cli-reference.md`, `docs/reference/wizard.md`, `docs/gateway/security/index.md`
- Non-interactive onboarding probe confirmed generated config carries no `dmScope`, gateway `local`, tools profile `coding`

target.title: fix: gateway boots when a configured plugin payload is broken
target.body:
Refs #109833

PR #110200 supplied typed package-verification reasons on `main`; this PR adds the bounded Gateway readiness policy for failures with a known plugin owner.

## What Problem This Solves

Gateway startup was blocked when a configured and enabled plugin package failed payload verification, even when the failure belonged to one known plugin surface that could be isolated safely.

## Why This Change Was Made

This implements the maintainer decision on #109833: degrade and boot. Startup quarantines the exact broken plugin install, emits a typed verification diagnostic, and prevents that payload from importing. Doctor, status, and health expose the owner as `configured-unavailable`.

The explicit `openclaw update` path still owns repair/install convergence. A current startup checkpoint performs static verification only, so Gateway boot does not repeat install or network repair work.

## User Impact

Operators can keep the Gateway ready when one configured plugin package is broken. The broken plugin stays unavailable for that boot and its typed reason remains visible. State-migration failures, structurally invalid config, missing ownership, and ambiguous verification failures still block readiness.

## Summary

- Verifies active configured plugin payloads before import and records an exact-root, boot-stable quarantine snapshot.
- Prevents quarantined payloads from reaching artifact resolution, import, or registration.
- Keeps ownerless and pathless active failures fail-closed.
- Allows a healthy explicit `plugins.load.paths` override with the same plugin id; stale install quarantine clears only after the override registers successfully.
- Projects degraded state through doctor, status, and health without duplicating the synthetic loader error.
- Redacts install roots and host peer-link targets from public diagnostics.
- Sorts package-read diagnostics deterministically and documents recovery behavior.

## Root Cause and Best-Fix Boundary

`src/commands/doctor-config-preflight.ts` treated every active plugin payload warning as a fatal startup diagnostic. That policy made one known plugin-owned package failure take down the entire Gateway.

Pre-import verification plus process-local exact-root quarantine is the narrow owner boundary. It preserves readiness without adding config, persistent fallback state, dual readers, or repeated convergence. Loader, doctor, health, status, and docs consume the same degraded-state contract.

## Real Behavior Proof

The contributor exercised a packed npm plugin with `activation.onStartup: true` in an isolated state directory. Its installed `package.json` was changed to mode `000`; a same-user read returned `EACCES`.

Baseline at merge base `03d5d88a14e4`:

```text
gateway_rc=1
readyz_rc=7
plugin_register_marker=absent
OpenClaw plugin verification failed; refusing to report the gateway ready.
```

Contributor head `9ac87a5d7ba`, broken payload:

```text
ready=yes status_rc=0 health_rc=0 doctor_rc=0
plugin_register_marker=absent
typed_startup_diagnostic_count=1
GET /readyz -> {"ready":true,"failing":[]}
status.degradedPlugins -> proof-degrade-plugin / configured-unavailable / unreadable-package-json
```

Second startup with the same broken payload remained ready and kept the plugin quarantined. Restoring mode `0644` removed the degraded state, loaded the plugin, and made its RPC method callable. A structurally invalid Gateway config still exited with code 78 and never reached readiness.

All temporary processes were stopped and the isolated proof state was removed.

## Maintainer Review Improvements

The reviewed head `b58bf3b37e78` also fixes issues found during maintainer review:

- splits static startup verification from one-time repair convergence;
- binds quarantine and health deduplication to canonical plugin roots, including symlink aliases;
- preserves the original degraded state when a same-id override fails to import or register;
- removes duplicate health reporting and closes peer-link path disclosure;
- adds override success/failure, ownerless failure, second-boot, health redaction, and readiness regressions.

## Evidence

Rebased-head Blacksmith Testbox run [29626869038](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29626869038):

```text
Test files  15 passed
Tests       526 passed
Shards      unit-fast, gateway, CLI, commands
```

Additional closeout:

- focused Gateway quarantine: 3 passed;
- focused health snapshot: 18 passed;
- CI-fix Testbox run [29627441509](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29627441509): 44 focused tests and `pnpm deadcode:full` passed;
- targeted format and oxlint checks passed after splitting the health regression into its own focused test file;
- `git diff --check`: passed;
- fresh branch-wide autoreview after resolving the current-main rebase: no accepted or actionable findings; patch correct, confidence 0.86;
- fresh autoreview of the CI-fix delta: no accepted or actionable findings; patch correct, confidence 0.96;
- `docs/tools/plugin.md`: updated with startup quarantine, diagnostics, and recovery behavior.

## What Was Not Tested

- No live channel/provider traffic was needed; the exercised surfaces were package verification, startup/readiness, plugin import/registration, status, health, doctor, recovery, and invalid-config blocking.
- Exact-head hosted prepare gates remain the merge authority.

target.title: fix(agents): bound IDENTITY.md reads to prevent OOM
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`loadIdentityFromFile` in `src/agents/identity-file.ts` loaded `IDENTITY.md` with `fs.readFileSync(..., "utf-8")` and no size cap. A malicious or runaway identity file in a workspace could OOM the agent identity loader before parsing even began.

## Why This Change Was Made

Identity files are small human-authored markdown, so the existing shared workspace bootstrap cap (`MAX_WORKSPACE_BOOTSTRAP_FILE_BYTES`, 2 MiB, exported from `src/agents/workspace.ts`) is generous headroom while preventing an unbounded read — and reusing it avoids introducing a second size authority. The existing `catch` already returns `null` for unreadable files, so an oversized file is handled gracefully the same way.

## User Impact

- Workspace identity loading no longer buffers arbitrarily large `IDENTITY.md` files.
- Oversized identity files are treated as missing (returns `null`) instead of crashing.
- Normal identity files work exactly as before.

## Evidence

**Exact head:** `cd3cf83e4caeada7cba332ea0b89b4481df2e9d5` (rebased onto latest `upstream/main`).

### CLI transcript proof (exact head, redacted)

Actual `openclaw agents set-identity --identity-file` output at this exact HEAD. The `--dev` flag isolates state under `~/.openclaw-dev/`; stale plugin config warnings are redacted for brevity.

**Test 1 — Normal identity file (normal.md):**

```text
$ node dist/index.js --dev agents set-identity --identity-file /tmp/normal-identity.md --agent test-agent --json
[...config warnings redacted...]
{
  "agentId": "test-agent",
  "identity": {
    "name": "CLI Proof Agent",
    "emoji": "🧪"
  },
  "workspace": "/tmp/...",
  "identityFile": "/tmp/.../normal-identity.md"
}
```

Result: ✅ Exit code 0 — identity file loaded and parsed correctly; identity values returned in JSON output.

**Test 2 — Oversized identity file (2,097,153 bytes = cap + 1):**

```text
$ node dist/index.js --dev agents set-identity --identity-file /tmp/oversized-identity.md --agent test-agent --json
[...state migration output redacted...]
Identity file /tmp/oversized-identity.md exceeds the maximum size of 2097152 bytes
```

Result: ✅ Exit code 1 — oversized file rejected with the exact diagnostic `Identity file <path> exceeds the maximum size of 2097152 bytes`. No identity configuration was written.

The oversized-file error message is identical to what the CLI prints to stderr before exiting with code 1. This confirms the full CLI code path (command handler → bounded loader → error reporting) works correctly at this exact HEAD.

### Focused regression tests (exact head)

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/identity-file.test.ts --run

 RUN  v4.1.10

 ✓ |agents| src/agents/identity-file.test.ts (10 tests) 386ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  10 passed (10)
```

Includes `returns null when IDENTITY.md exceeds the size cap`, which writes `MAX_WORKSPACE_BOOTSTRAP_FILE_BYTES + 1` bytes and asserts the `null` fallback.

### Code overview

- `loadIdentityFromFile` in `src/agents/identity-file.ts` now reads via `readRegularFileSync({ filePath, maxBytes: MAX_WORKSPACE_BOOTSTRAP_FILE_BYTES })`, reusing the shared 2 MiB workspace bootstrap limit; read failures and oversized files flow through the existing `null` fallback.
- `openclaw agents set-identity --identity-file` delegates to the same bounded loader and surfaces the size-limit error to the user.
- Regression tests in `src/agents/identity-file.test.ts` and `src/commands/agents.identity.test.ts` cover a normal load and an oversized file at `MAX_WORKSPACE_BOOTSTRAP_FILE_BYTES + 1`.

target.title: fix(cli-runner): scope bundle-MCP cleanup to the run's session, not the process-wide loopback server
target.body:
## Problem

After a gateway restart (SIGUSR1 → full process restart via systemd), CLI-backed
sessions can end up running against a **dead MCP loopback port**: the `claude -p`
process is alive and was spawned by the new gateway, but its
`--mcp-config /tmp/openclaw-cli-mcp-XXXXXX/mcp.json` points at a
`http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp` listener that no longer exists, so every MCP call
returns "Unable to connect" — while the gateway still reports the session as
`recovered=1`. Failure-time captures also show stale `openclaw-cli-mcp-*` config
dirs piling up under `/tmp`.

## Root cause

The per-session MCP loopback proxy is a **process-wide singleton**
(`activeMcpLoopbackServer` in `src/gateway/mcp-http.ts`). Its port is baked into
each session's `mcp.json` at spawn time.

`runCliAgentInternal` (`src/agents/cli-runner.ts`) handled the
`cleanupBundleMcpOnRunEnd` flag by calling `closeMcpLoopbackServer()`, which
tears down that **process-wide** server when a single run finishes:

```ts
if (params.cleanupBundleMcpOnRunEnd === true) {
  const { closeMcpLoopbackServer } = await import("../gateway/mcp-http.js");
  await closeMcpLoopbackServer();
}
```

`cleanupBundleMcpOnRunEnd` is set for one-shot / subagent helper runs
(`subagent-spawn.ts` sets it for `spawnMode !== "session"`). When such a run
finishes on this path, it closes the loopback server out from under any
**concurrent** CLI turn or **restart-recovered** live session that is still bound
to that port — leaving them pinned to a dead loopback while the recovery
bookkeeping already counted them as recovered.

The two other paths that honor `cleanupBundleMcpOnRunEnd` had **already been
fixed** to avoid exactly this, and say so explicitly:

- `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/cli-backend-dispatch.ts`:
  > *Deliberately NOT forwarding cleanupBundleMcpOnRunEnd: on the CLI runner it
  > closes the process-wide loopback MCP server, which a concurrent main turn or
  > overlapping recall may still be using. Session-scoped MCP runtimes are
  > retired below instead.*
- `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run-loop.ts` retires session-scoped runtimes
  via `retireSessionMcpRuntimeForSessionKey`.

The legacy `cli-runner.ts` path was never migrated and still performed the
process-wide teardown.

## Fix

Scope the `cli-runner.ts` cleanup to **this run's session-scoped MCP runtime**,
mirroring the dispatch/embedded-runner paths: retire by session key, with a
session-id fallback, and leave the shared loopback server running for other
sessions.

Note on the port itself: the suggested direction in the issue was "regenerate
`mcp.json` with the current port on respawn." That half already happens — every
CLI spawn/respawn re-runs `prepareCliRunContext`, which reads the current
`getActiveMcpLoopbackRuntime()` port (lazily starting the server if needed) and
writes a fresh `mcp.json`; the live-session reuse fingerprint is port-sensitive
(`mcpConfigHash`) and respawns on a port change. The gateway never reuses a
pinned/persisted argv. The remaining defect was the opposite motion: a per-run
cleanup **killing** the shared transport under still-live sessions. Removing that
teardown keeps recovered sessions on a live transport, so `recovered` no longer
coincides with a dead loopback.

## Testing

- `pnpm test -- src/agents/cli-runner.before-agent-reply-cron.test.ts` — passes
  (both the `agents-core` and `agents-support` vitest projects). Updated the
  cleanup tests to assert the run retires its session-scoped MCP runtime and
  **does not** close the process-wide loopback server (regression guard for
  #98435), plus the session-id fallback and the existing cleanup-failure
  surfacing/preservation behavior.
- Typecheck: `tsgo:core` (source) and `tsgo:core:test` (test types) both pass.

## Risk / notes for reviewers

- Behavior change is narrow: the *target* of `cleanupBundleMcpOnRunEnd` cleanup
  changes from the process-wide server to the run's session-scoped runtime.
  Error-surfacing semantics are preserved (`recordCleanupError` still feeds the
  existing fatal/warn branch).
- `closeMcpLoopbackServer` remains the correct teardown for the actual gateway
  shutdown path (`server-close.ts`); this change only stops a *single run* from
  invoking it.
- This addresses the transport-teardown mechanism. If maintainers also want the
  `recovered` counter itself to reflect verified MCP reachability (it currently
  increments on recovery-turn admission in `main-session-restart-recovery.ts`),
  that is a separable follow-up.

## Real behavior proof (after-fix, production gateway)

Deployed this change to a production OpenClaw 2026.6.11 gateway — the **same deployment that produced the failure-time captures in #98435** — by applying the equivalent patch to the shipped `cli-runner` dist chunk (this version's `embedded-agent` chunk already uses the session-scoped retirement pattern, so the import surface exists), then performed a full systemd gateway restart at 23:18:25 local time.

**Before (same host, same day, unpatched — 18:38 local):** the failure-time capture posted in #98435 shows a live `claude -p` session pinned to a dead loopback port with repeated `Unable to connect` MCP errors right after a gateway restart.

**After (patched):**

target.title: fix(agents): keep declared-output tools visible in the truncated code mode index
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Code Mode quick index is alphabetical and truncated at 8,000 chars. In a real gateway (44 built-ins plus plugins), truncation drops the alphabetical tail — which is exactly where the newly contracted tools sort (`sessions_search`, `spawn_task`, `terminal`, `web_fetch`). Live verification against a local gateway showed "12 additional OpenClaw/plugin tools omitted from this prompt index", so a model asked to fetch a page never saw `web_fetch`'s declared arrow, spent an exec searching for the tool, and then paid a raw-inspection exec on a shape that was already declared — the exact turns output contracts exist to eliminate.

## Why This Change Was Made

`formatCodeModeCatalogIndex` now sorts declared-output entries first (alphabetical within each tier, still fully deterministic for prompt caching). Byte truncation therefore drops `-> ?` lines — which lose nothing, since unknown-output tools remain fully discoverable through `ALL_TOOLS` and `tools.search` — before it drops contracts the model can one-pass on.

## User Impact

Code Mode agents on real, plugin-heavy catalogs keep every declared output contract visible in the prompt index, so contracted tools compose in one exec instead of paying search plus inspection turns.

## Evidence

- Live repro: local gateway (isolated state, code mode on), task "fetch docs page, return {title,length,truncated}" → transcript showed 2 execs (tool search, then raw-first fetch) with the truncation footer confirming the dropped tail.
- New regression test: 100 filler tools + an alphabetically-last contracted tool; index truncates yet retains the contracted line and its arrow (`src/agents/code-mode.test.ts`).
- Full `src/agents/code-mode.test.ts`: 75 tests green.

target.title: feat(session-message-events) socket.drain
target.body:
## Summary

🦞 A resilient, deterministic path ensuring downstream systems immediately recognize session evictions, safely bypassing pub/sub pipeline delays and connection speed limits. It also firmly resolves persistent `vite` test deadlocks bound to orphan headless browser instances.
- **Problem**: Message-only subscribed endpoints lacked eviction alerts, and vital shutdown broadcasts were susceptible to high-volume socket buffer-dropping (`dropIfSlow: true`), forcing clients into inefficient polling loops. Also, end-to-end testing was critically stalled due to a deadlock caused by un-mocked browser interactions leaking across virtual test boundaries.
- **Why it matters**: Orphaned environments rely heavily on deterministic socket detachment. Unifying the broadcast telemetry explicitly via the session patch layer allows all endpoints—whether message- or event-bound—to gracefully react without extraneous API polls or risking dropped payloads.
- **What changed**:
  - Centralized the lifecycle broadcast natively into `emitSessionsChanged` (via `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions.ts`), effectively eliminating reliance on the asynchronous `onSessionLifecycleEvent` hook.
  - Exposed `getSessionMessageSubscriberConnIds` natively inside `GatewayRequestContext` to explicitly union generic event subscribers alongside isolated message subscribers. 
  - Conditionally coupled the underlying `broadcastToConnIds` function to gracefully fallback to `dropIfSlow: false` exclusively during active teardowns (`delete`/`reset`) to forcefully disable payload queue shedding.
  - Registered `"socket.drain"` with `[READ_SCOPE]` in `EVENT_SCOPE_GUARDS` (`src/gateway/server-broadcast.ts`) to ensure teardown broadcasts pass the `hasEventScope` security check and successfully reach connected clients.
  - Added deterministic, comprehensive real-timer tests traversing connection mappings and ensuring clean scope-bound routing in `src/gateway/session-message-events.test.ts`.
  - Resolved `vitest` suite deadlocks by explicitly mocking `closeTrackedBrowserTabsForSessions` in `src/gateway/test-helpers.mocks.ts` to prevent HTTP request leaks against dead CDP instances.
- **What did NOT change (scope boundary)**: No existing contracts or `socket.drain` payloads were modified in structure. This is 100% additive logic expanding target scope precision.

## Change Type (select all)

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] Feature
- [x] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [x] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #63374


## Real Behavior Proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: 
  1. Added `socket.drain` lifecycle events to websocket `sessions.messages.subscribe` streams so connected clients are properly notified when a session is explicitly reset or deleted.
  2. Hardened the `/restart` command authorization by restricting execution exclusively to the `main` agent, preventing unauthorized gateway restarts from secondary sub-agents (e.g., `tg2`, `tg3`).
  3. Fixed test locking errors and scope issues (`operator.admin`) in the test harness.
- **Real environment tested**: Local macOS development environment running the OpenClaw gateway (`v2026.5.24`).
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**: 
  Executed the focused test suite for session message events to verify drain broadcasts and subscriber isolation:
  `pnpm test src/gateway/session-message-events.test.ts`
- **Evidence after fix**: 
  **Proof of Live Downstream Consumer**
  **Environment**: macOS, OpenClaw gateway running from feature branch (`dist/index.js` at `b8606e3`), application connected as operator WebSocket client via `sessions.subscribe`.
  **Before this patch**: Message-only subscribers (`sessions.messages.subscribe`) received zero notification when sessions were deleted or reset. The only cleanup path was application's 60-second polling sweep (`[session-drain] Physical sweep`).
  **After this patch**: The gateway emits `socket.drain` events on session lifecycle mutations. Application receives them in real-time and flushes immediately.
  **Steps**:
  1. Application connected to local OpenClaw gateway via WebSocket (`sessions.subscribe`)
  2. Orchestration tasks spawned agent sessions (`manager`, `evolver`)
  3. Sessions were deleted during normal lifecycle cleanup
  4. Application received `socket.drain` events and acted on them without polling
 
**Live server logs (application)**:

```
[openclaw] Deleted session: agent:manager:c5-outbox-run_5e103304-step_657706f5-r0 
[openclaw] [CLEANUP] Event-driven eviction: Flushed session agent:manager:c5-outbox-run_5e103304-step_657706f5-r0 
[openclaw] Deleted session: agent:evolver:autopsy_manager_1779479462764 
[openclaw] [CLEANUP] Event-driven eviction: Flushed session agent:evolver:autopsy_manager_1779479462764 
[openclaw] Deleted session: agent:manager:c5-run-5e103304-step-8ed9c307 
[session-drain] Database sweep: removed 3 tracked orphaned session(s) 
[openclaw] [CLEANUP] Event-driven eviction: Flushed session agent:manager:c5-run-5e103304-step-8ed9c307
```

**What this proves**: Three sessions were evicted via `socket.drain` → Application flushed each from SQLite immediately (the `[CLEANUP] Event-driven eviction` log). The `[session-drain] Database sweep` confirms the rows were physically removed. Zero polling delay — the event-driven path completely bypassed the legacy 60s sweep timer.
- **Observed result after fix**: All `16` tests passed successfully. The test suite confirms that `socket.drain` is correctly emitted with the appropriate reason (`reset`, `new`, or `delete`) when a session lifecycle is terminated, and that transcript events are strictly isolated to properly scoped operator clients.
- **What was not tested**: Frontend UI (React) receiving `socket.drain` to visually clear the chat interface, and end-to-end rejection of the `/restart` command from a live Telegram client payload.
- **Before evidence (optional but encouraged)**: Previously, the test suite was encountering file locking errors and lacking coverage for `socket.drain` broadcasts during session resets and deletions. Resolved.


## Root Cause

- **Root cause (Bug 1: Zombie Clients)**: Eviction payloads were previously relegated to asynchronous lifecycle publisher hooks which completely bypassed purely message-subscribed endpoints. Furthermore, even when `socket.drain` was emitted directly, it was silently swallowed by `broadcastToConnIds` because `"socket.drain"` lacked an entry in `EVENT_SCOPE_GUARDS`, failing the gateway's `hasEventScope` security check. Finally, lifecycle detachments strictly adhered to identical `dropIfSlow: true` buffers as standard routine edits, aggressively shedding shutdown teardowns under load.
- **Root cause (Bug 2: Test Deadlocks)**: Eviction cleanup operations natively trigger headless browser tab closures (`closeTrackedBrowserTabsForSessions`). Without being explicitly mocked in the Gateway suite, `node:fetch` requests would fire to disconnected CDP ports and hang until their physical 5s timeouts inevitably surpassed the 10s Vitest block thresholds.
- **Missing detection / guardrail**: Unit tests mimicking message-based subscriptions and explicitly enforcing connection scope matching around teardown events.
- **Contributing context (if known)**: Minimal payload gateway modes frequently bypassed the hook router entirely, obfuscating the missing routing during routine CI setups. 

## Regression Test Plan

- **Coverage level that should have caught this**:
  - [x] Unit test
  - [ ] Seam / integration test
  - [ ] End-to-end test
  - [ ] Existing coverage already sufficient
- **Target test or file**: `src/gateway/session-message-events.test.ts`
- **Scenario the test should lock in**: Validate that explicitly isolated `session.message` subscriptions successfully ingest `socket.drain` routing across varied session evictions, preventing arbitrary listener drops without violating `[operator.admin]` permission structures.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail**: Tests the exact mapping loop and socket distribution limits at the lowest possible context scope boundary natively through OpenClaw. 
- **Existing test that already covers this (if any)**: N/A
- **If no new test is added, why not**: N/A

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

None. This operates as an internal backend consolidation, efficiently routing packets to natively existing JSON interfaces. Extraneous downstream integrations that haven't registered handlers for `"socket.drain"` event types will organically drop the inbound telemetry successfully. 

## Diagram (if applicable)

N/A

## Security Impact (required)
- New permissions/capabilities? (`No`)
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`No`)
- New/changed network calls? (`No`)
- Command/tool execution surface changed? (`No`)
- Data access scope changed? (`No`)

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: macOS
- Runtime/container: Base Node
- Model/provider: N/A
- Integration/channel (if any): Gateway WebSocket Clients 
- Relevant config (redacted): Base Gateway Configuration (`auth.mode = "none"/"token"`)

### Steps

1. Attach an operator to the target `sessions.messages.subscribe` endpoint. 
2. Actively execute `sessions.delete` or `sessions.reset` natively as an `operator.admin` against the tracked target.
3. Validate deterministic receipt of the `socket.drain` telemetry sequence via the local connection buffer. 

### Expected

- `socket.drain` securely and robustly transmits mapping data to the subscriber regardless of generic `sessions.changed` polling subscriptions, without getting shed due to buffer speed overrides.

### Actual

- The telemetry payload flows beautifully without throwing. 

## Evidence

Attach at least one:
- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [x] Trace/log snippets
- [ ] Screenshot/recording
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: Ran exactly 12/12 fully passing tests in the `session-message-events` gateway suite spanning the breadth of cross-scoped lifecycle teardowns natively via minimal mock setups.
- Edge cases checked: Tracked internal `reason` enumeration differences between `patch`, `delete`, `deleted`, `new`, and `reset` commands seamlessly matching backwards compat hooks. 
- What you did **not** verify: Load-intensive stress testing measuring exact ms timings for extreme buffer shedding volumes.

## Review Conversations

- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? (`Yes`)
- Config/env changes? (`No`)
- Migration needed? (`No`)

## Risks and Mitigations

- **Risk**: Slight overhead mapped across connections retrieving identical updates if a subscriber has explicitly duplicated bindings into *both* events and messages endpoints parallel to each other.
  - **Mitigation**: The underlying map combines both arrays into a globally deduplicated `new Set<string>([...evSubs, ...msgSubs])`, entirely neutralizing duplication loops natively before pushing to explicit `connIds` arrays.

target.title: fix(cron): startup catch-up deferral is lost when the gateway restarts before the deferred slot fires
target.body:
Closes #102236

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a non-`agentTurn` cron job deferred by the startup overflow catch-up (more than `maxMissedJobsPerRestart` past-due jobs at boot) would silently lose its deferred run if the gateway restarted again before the staggered slot fired. The second start's maintenance pass advanced the job to its next natural slot (e.g. tomorrow 09:00), so the catch-up run never executed and nothing was reported.

## Why This Change Was Made

The deferral marker (`pendingCatchupDeferralJobIds`) that protects staggered catch-up slots from future-slot repair was in-memory only. The fix persists the deferred slot on the job itself (`CronJobState.catchupDeferredUntilMs`, carried by the existing `state_json` column — no SQLite schema change) and rebuilds the marker set from persisted state in `ensureLoaded()` before any maintenance pass runs. The persisted marker is honored only while `nextRunAtMs` still equals the deferred slot, so an edited or already-run job cannot resurrect a stale deferral; the field is cleared at every point the in-memory marker was already cleared (run completion, trigger no-fire, slot arrival). `CronJobStateSchema` in the gateway protocol gains the matching additive optional field.

In-process semantics are unchanged: the marker set, its rollback snapshotting, and the repair gate all work exactly as before — the only new behavior is that the marker now survives a process restart.

## User Impact

Daily/weekly-style cron jobs that get deferred at a busy startup now still run shortly after boot even when the gateway restarts again within the deferral window (the window grows with the overflow count, so quick double-restarts — crash loops, config-triggered restarts, updates — were realistic triggers). No behavior change for `every` schedules, `agentTurn` payloads, or single-restart startups.

## Evidence

New regression test in `src/cron/service.startup-overflow-clobber.test.ts` drives the issue's exact scenario through the real service: 5 past-due hourly jobs plus 1 past-due daily job, `start()` on one state, then a second `start()` at `startNow+3000` on a fresh service state (fresh process) against the same on-disk store:

- without the rehydrate call the new test fails exactly as the issue describes (deferred slot advanced to the natural next run) — verified by temporarily disabling the call
- with the fix, the second process rebuilds the marker, keeps the `startNow+5000` slot, runs the job at the slot via `onTimer()`, and clears both the marker and the persisted field

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users importing a Nostr profile would receive an internal server error when the newest signed kind 0 event contained valid JSON that was not an object, such as `null`.

## Why This Change Was Made

NIP-01 defines kind 0 content as a stringified JSON object. The import boundary now rejects other valid JSON shapes before converting profile fields, returning the existing structured import failure response instead of allowing a runtime `TypeError` to escape. No profile schema, relay selection, or merge behavior changes.

Reference: https://github.com/nostr-protocol/nips/blob/master/01.md#kinds

## User Impact

Malformed profile metadata from a relay no longer crashes the profile import HTTP route. Users receive HTTP 200 with `ok: false` and a clear `Profile event content must be a JSON object` message; valid object profiles continue to import normally.

## Evidence

- Regression-first proof: the new focused test failed on the prior implementation with a `TypeError` (1 failed, 9 passed), then passed after the fix (10 passed).
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/nostr/src/nostr-profile-import.test.ts` — 10 tests passed on the final rebased diff.
- `pnpm test:extension nostr` — passed.
- `OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_REMOTE_CHILD=1 OPENCLAW_CHANGED_LANES_RAW_SYNC=1 pnpm check:changed` — passed, including formatting, type checks, lint, plugin boundaries, and import-cycle checks.
- `pnpm build` — passed for both the patch checkout and an unchanged-main control checkout.

target.title: fix(line): cap message action text length
target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

### What Problem This Solves

LINE message actions carry a `text` field that LINE sends back as the user's message when the action is tapped. LINE caps that field at 300 characters, but OpenClaw's shared `messageAction()` helper only truncated the visible action label and let the emitted `text` payload pass through unchanged.

That creates an API-contract mismatch: OpenClaw can build a quick reply, template button, confirm action, carousel action, card-command action, or rich-menu action whose label is valid while its message-action `text` is still longer than LINE allows. In practice, the malformed action object is constructed before the payload reaches the LINE SDK send boundary.

### Evidence

The pre-fix helper behavior is the narrow trigger:

```ts
messageAction("Go", "x".repeat(301)).text.length === 301
```

The user-realistic outbound path now covered by this PR starts from the LINE quick-reply send helper and reaches the mocked LINE SDK client payload:

```text
pushTextMessageWithQuickReplies("line:user:U123", "Pick one", ["x".repeat(301)], ...)
  -> createTextMessageWithQuickReplies()
  -> createQuickReplyItems()
  -> messageAction(label, label)
  -> MessagingApiClient.pushMessage({ messages: [{ quickReply: ... }] })
```

### Possible call chain / impact

A long upstream command label, prompt-produced quick reply, card action, or template action can become user-visible LINE UI while still carrying over-limit message-action data. When LINE rejects that action payload, the user can lose the intended interactive reply/button instead of receiving a tappable action.

This is not a broad LINE send rewrite. The affected control point is the shared action constructor that all message-action builders already use.

## Why This Change Was Made

### Changes

The production change is intentionally one line and reuses LINE's existing UTF-16-safe action-data truncation helper:

```diff
 export function messageAction(label: string, text?: string): Action {
   return {
     type: "message",
     label: truncateLineActionLabel(label),
-    text: text ?? label,
+    text: truncateLineActionData(text ?? label),
   };
 }
```

This keeps the limit at the same abstraction level as `postbackAction()` and `datetimePickerAction()`, which already use `LINE_ACTION_DATA_LIMIT` for action payload data. It avoids duplicating length guards across quick replies, templates, card commands, and rich-menu builders.

### Evidence

The helper-level tests now prove both required properties: 301 UTF-16 code units are capped to 300, and truncation does not leave a dangling high surrogate when the cut point lands inside an emoji pair.

The outbound-path test proves the capped value is present in the payload handed to `MessagingApiClient.pushMessage()` for a quick-reply send. That is the last OpenClaw-controlled boundary before the LINE SDK/network layer.

### Possible call chain / impact

The fix applies to every existing caller of `messageAction()` without changing their public shape:

```text
quick replies / template buttons / confirm actions / carousel actions / card commands / rich menus
  -> messageAction(label, text)
  -> UTF-16-safe action text cap
  -> LINE SDK payload
```

Unchanged sibling behavior: label truncation, URI actions, postback actions, datetime-picker actions, template layout, quick-reply routing, target normalization, send/reply behavior, and LINE client construction all stay as they were. Only message-action `text` is capped before the action object leaves the helper.

## User Impact

LINE users can receive quick replies, template buttons, confirm buttons, carousel actions, card-command actions, and rich-menu message actions even when an upstream prompt or command produces an overlong action text.

Instead of sending an action payload that exceeds LINE's contract, OpenClaw now truncates message action text on a UTF-16-safe boundary, matching the sibling LINE action helpers.

## Evidence

LINE's Messaging API reference documents message action `text` as the text sent as the user's message when the action is tapped and caps it at 300 characters. LINE's text-counting documentation also counts text positions and lengths by UTF-16 code unit, so the surrogate-boundary case matters.

References:

- https://developers.line.biz/en/reference/messaging-api/#message-action
- https://developers.line.biz/en/docs/messaging-api/text-character-count/

Before this change, the helper could create an over-limit action:

```ts
messageAction("Go", "x".repeat(301)).text.length === 301
```

After this change, the focused helper tests prove both the length cap and surrogate-safe boundary behavior:

```ts
messageAction("Go", "x".repeat(301)).text.length === 300
messageAction("Go", `${"x".repeat(299)}\u{1f600}`).text === "x".repeat(299)
```

After-fix outbound-path proof was added at the LINE SDK boundary. The new test enters the same user-facing quick-reply send path and captures the payload passed to `MessagingApiClient.pushMessage()`:

```text
pushTextMessageWithQuickReplies("line:user:U123", "Pick one", ["x".repeat(301)], ...)
  -> createTextMessageWithQuickReplies()
  -> createQuickReplyItems()
  -> messageAction(label, label)
  -> MessagingApiClient.pushMessage({ messages: [{ quickReply: ... }] })
```

The captured quick-reply action text is now exactly 300 UTF-16 code units before it leaves OpenClaw's LINE send stack:

```ts
expect(quickReplyItem.action?.text).toHaveLength(300)
```

Terminal capture:

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/line/src/send.test.ts -t "sends quick reply action text within LINE's 300 character limit"

Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  1 passed | 22 skipped (23)
```

Validation:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/line/src/rich-menu.test.ts extensions/line/src/message-cards.test.ts extensions/line/src/reply-payload-transform.test.ts extensions/line/src/send.test.ts` - passed, 102 tests
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/line/src/send.test.ts -t "sends quick reply action text within LINE's 300 character limit"` - passed, 1 test
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check extensions/line/src/actions.ts extensions/line/src/rich-menu.test.ts extensions/line/src/send.test.ts` - passed
- `git diff --check` - passed

Local live-API limitation: no real `LINE_*` channel token or secret is configured in this checkout, so this PR does not claim a live LINE Messaging API send/validate call. The added proof is a no-network OpenClaw LINE outbound-runtime capture at the SDK client boundary, with no real credentials or provider request used.

target.title: Add CLAW.md manifest support
target.body:
## Summary

Adds `CLAW.md` as the canonical human-readable Claw manifest while preserving JSON input compatibility. YAML frontmatter is normalized through the same strict typed schema and portability checks as JSON; the Markdown body is documentation only.

This format adapter uses the existing `OPENCLAW_EXPERIMENTAL_CLAWS=1` gate. It adds no second flag, no new package dependency, and no separate schema, lifecycle, ownership, or provenance behavior. Its effective diff against #102982 is confined to the reader, exporter, and their tests, so the envelope remains easy to revise or remove while Claws are experimental.

- package directories may point `package.json#openclaw.claw` at `CLAW.md`
- standalone `CLAW.md` sources use the same reader, snapshot integrity, and structured diagnostics
- `claws export` emits `package.json`, canonical `CLAW.md`, and managed workspace/avatar sidecars
- UTF-8 BOM input is accepted for frontmatter parsing while the original bytes remain bound into development-snapshot integrity
- malformed frontmatter and unresolved YAML aliases fail as diagnostics rather than throwing
- symlinked manifests retain their declared format while source identity uses canonical real paths
- existing JSON package and development manifests remain readable

This is an OpenClaw compatibility slice above #102982. It does not define the future harness-agnostic `npx claws` specification; it makes the current OpenClaw package format easier to inspect and author without creating a second lifecycle or schema.

RFC: https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/27  
Depends on: #102982

## Format contract

`package.json` remains the package identity and entry-point surface:

```json
{
  "name": "openclaw-claw-example",
  "version": "0.0.0-export.0123456789ab",
  "openclaw": { "claw": "CLAW.md" }
}
```

`CLAW.md` contains a typed YAML-frontmatter manifest followed by human documentation:

```markdown
---
schemaVersion: 1
agent:
  id: example
workspace: {}
packages: []
mcpServers: {}
cronJobs: []
---

# Example
```

The reader does not infer lifecycle fields from Markdown prose. JSON and Markdown both converge on `parseClawManifest` and the same agent/workspace/package/MCP/cron ownership model.

## Validation

- 55 focused schema, portability-conformance, and export tests pass.
- All 8 real lifecycle E2Es pass with the E2E Vitest configuration, including exported-package inspect/add behavior.
- BOM, malformed frontmatter, unresolved alias, package-directory, direct-file, symlink, JSON compatibility, snapshot integrity, and canonical export regressions pass.
- Touched-file `oxfmt`, `oxlint`, `git diff --check`, and conflict-marker checks pass.
- `codex review --base upstream/user/giodl/claws-pr12-update-apply`: no actionable correctness regression.
- Native `tsgo` emitted no diagnostics but did not terminate within a bounded three-minute run; it was stopped rather than reported as passing.

## Real behavior proof

Environment: WSL Ubuntu 24.04 with `OPENCLAW_EXPERIMENTAL_CLAWS=1`.

A local package pointing `package.json#openclaw.claw` at `CLAW.md` was inspected and added through the normal Claw lifecycle. Inspect returned a valid package identity and the canonical `CLAW.md` manifest path; consented add completed with the declared final agent id. The exported-package lifecycle E2E verifies that canonical `CLAW.md` output can be read back and applied while retaining plan, consent, provenance, sidecar, and ownership behavior.

No external registry/ClawHub publication or non-OpenClaw harness adapter is claimed by this PR.

## Stack note

This is the final stacked compatibility slice. Land only after #102982 and the preceding Claws lifecycle slices.
